human_tolerance.notes: Lives in a semi-domesticated state around human habitations, forages around settlements and is often fed by people. Wikipedia reports that it congregates near human habitats and feeds on food scraps.

phases.name: moult
phases.note: Wikipedia: the male's train feathers moult from the end of the monsoon in August or September and are fully developed by February to March.

vocalizations.description: Loud calls, with about seven known call variants, given frequently at dusk as birds arrive at roost sites.
Loud alarm calls, with about six known alarm variants, given by both sexes when a predator is near; birds call frequently at dusk as they arrive at roost sites and may call at night when alarmed.

conservation.iucn.note: Wikipedia: listed as Least Concern. Not checked against the IUCN page, which is not openly licensed.

range.native.note: Wikipedia: resident breeder across most of India and Sri Lanka. Pakistan, Nepal and Bangladesh are not listed because the source text does not name them as native countries.

traits.body_plan.note: Bird, two legs and wings, same convention as other Galliformes records.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of the male's stated 4.1-5.2 kg (Wikipedia Description) = 4.65 kg. Peahen 2.7-4.1 kg is included in mass_range_kg. The male is the modelled form.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Lower bound 2.7 kg is the peahen's stated minimum; upper bound 5.2 kg is the male's stated maximum (Wikipedia Description).

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the male's stated bill-to-tail length 100-120 cm (Wikipedia Description) = 110 cm. Excludes the train, which is 200-230 cm to its tip; the peahen is about 97 cm.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia (Lifespan and mortality): 'estimated to live for only about 15 years in the wild'; up to 23 years in captivity is a captive maximum and is not used. Disagreement: the Animal Diversity Web account gives an average of about 20 years in the wild, with 25 as a maximum. ADW is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 and was not used because a permissive source gives a typical wild value. The upstream source behind Wikipedia's figure was not identified; a maintainer should resolve the 15-versus-20 conflict.

traits.diet.note: Presence only, from Wikipedia Diet: grass, seeds, flowerbuds, fruits, insects and small reptiles, with cultivated grain and food scraps. The percentages are an authored allocation grouped by food class, not measured shares. browse 0.3 covers grass and flowerbuds; vertebrate 0.2 covers small reptiles and rodents (Behaviour and ecology); invertebrate 0.15 covers insects.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia: forages in small groups called musters, usually one peacock and three to five peahens. Group size 4-6 is derived from that count.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Wikipedia: found in the open early in the morning, rests under cover in the heat of the day, sighted dust-bathing at dusk and roosts in tall trees at night.

traits.defense.note: Wikipedia: escapes by running on foot through undergrowth when disturbed and rarely flies.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement, not a sourced value. Wikipedia says peafowl are common around human habitations and are sometimes fed, yet they still flee through undergrowth when disturbed.

traits.nest_type.note: Wikipedia Breeding section describes the clutch and incubation; the nest site is not stated in the sections read, so ground nesting is taken from the Galliformes convention and is unverified for this species.

traits.perching.note: Wikipedia: roosts on tall trees at night. Perching is an inference from roosting in trees.

habitat.note: Habitat use shares, resource weights and shelter_tag are authored from the Wikipedia habitat, diet and roosting statements. Weights are not measured.

range.note: Wikipedia Distribution: resident breeder in India and Sri Lanka; introduced and feral in many other parts of the world, which is not recorded as native range.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walk: forages and runs on foot. Fly: Wikipedia says it is capable of flight but rarely flies; Trot is omitted because biped_winged has no built-in trot animation.

traits.flight.note: Wikipedia Behaviour and ecology: despite its size it is capable of flight, with regular slow flaps.

traits.skin.note: Wikipedia Description: plumage of feathers, the defining feature of the species.

traits.size_class.note: Computed from mass_kg 4.65 using the schema's Medium band (1-50 kg).

traits.limb_count.note: Bird convention: two walking legs, wings not counted.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Bird convention: endotherm (Aves); not a species-specific measurement.

traits.metamorphosis.note: Bird convention: no metamorphosis; hatchlings resemble adults in form.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia Distribution calls it a resident breeder; no migration or dormancy is reported.

seasonal.phases.note: Moult, Aug to Mar: Wikipedia Description (moult starts at end of monsoon in Aug or Sep, fully developed by Feb to Mar). No breeding phase is recorded: Wikipedia ties breeding to the monsoon without a month range, and local Indian studies disagree (Kanha courtship late Jan to June; Viralimalai Oct to early Dec), so no defensible Indian breeding window was found.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Wikipedia Breeding: eggs are incubated by the female for about 28 to 30 days; the duration_days 29 is the midpoint.

behavior.note: Authored program choice. bt-ground-probing-bird-v1 is used: it probes the ground on foot for food, takes off and flies to a tree perch when threatened, roosts on a perch at night, and calls from a perch in the sun-elevation window it declares. Overrides: food_tag seed (one tag only), song call, alarm alarm. The nest-building window is left at the program default of months 10 to 12 and is UNRESOLVED: it matches the Viralimalai courtship record (Oct to early Dec, southern India) but not the Kanha record (courtship late Jan to June); the program has no way to disable nest-building except a valid month window, and no defensible Indian nesting window was found. This is a merge blocker. Limitations: the program makes every threat response a flight to a perch, whereas Wikipedia says the bird mostly escapes on foot and rarely flies; the midday shelter rest under cover, ground nesting and flock muster are not expressed; and the calling window follows the program's dawn-to-dusk sun condition, not the dusk and night calling Wikipedia describes.

vocalizations.note: Wikipedia: makes loud calls used to indicate a predator; calls frequently at dusk when arriving at roost; may call at night when alarmed; about six alarm variants. The call entry is the dusk call at roosts; the alarm entry is the predator alarm. Context is mapped to the program's call IDs; the call's loudness and cooldown are authored.

look.note: Authored blocky model for the previewer; palette and extra parts are judgement, not measurements. The train is modelled on the male.
